NXP FRDM i.MX 95 · eIQ GenAI Flow

The eIQ GenAI Flow, end to end

The exact screens an attendee moves through — sign up with a password, claim a board, then work the cockpit top to bottom in workshop order.

1 sign up→ 2 kit→ 3 claim→ 4 connected→ 5 cockpit · cards 1–6
Arrow keys advance · press N for presenter notes. Visual walkthrough companion to the concept deck (workshop-slides.html).

Create your account

One form, one password — your private slice of the platform, instantly

  • Name, email, company, event code — and choose your password right here
  • Setting a password skips the email invite — you're ready the moment you submit
  • One API chain underneath: a private entity, a user, an iMX95genai device with an x.509 cert
  • You only ever see your own board — isolation is the platform's, not the UI's
01 · SIGN UP02 · KIT03 · CLAIM04 · CONNECTED05 · COCKPIT
Everything here is the same public REST API a customer uses to onboard a fleet. The password rides the same create-user call, so no invite email is needed.

Your board kit

The kit IS your credentials — a real x.509 device identity

  • Log into the /IOTCONNECT management portal with the password you chose
  • Download the board kit (.zip): iotcDeviceConfig.json + x.509 cert + private key
  • Board on USB? The finder reads its IP over the serial console — or use the manual steps
01 · SIGN UP02 · KIT03 · CLAIM04 · CONNECTED05 · COCKPIT
The three files in the kit are exactly what authenticates the board over mutual-TLS MQTT — the same identity mechanism a production device ships with.

Claim your board

A page the board serves itself — drag, drop, claimed

  • Open the board's own URL from its card — http://imx95-XXXX.local:8088
  • Drag the kit on → identity installs, demo restarts → “✓ Connected”
  • Re-claiming needs explicit confirmation — no accidental board theft
01 · SIGN UP02 · KIT03 · CLAIM04 · CONNECTED05 · COCKPIT
The claim page is served locally by the board on port 8088 — no cloud round-trip to install identity.

Watch it come online

The board finds its broker itself and streams — the production pipeline, not a mock

  • The board found its broker and credentials itself at boot
  • Template = the contract: 54 telemetry attributes, 18 commands
  • D2C: ~50 attributes every 10 s over MQTT · C2D: every button is a real, acknowledged command
01 · SIGN UP02 · KIT03 · CLAIM04 · CONNECTED05 · COCKPIT
The full hop is laptop -> REST API -> C2D command (MQTT) -> board runs the model -> D2C telemetry -> dashboard. Same pipeline a fleet of thousands uses.

Sign in to your cockpit

The same account you created at signup — scoped to your board

  • Log in with the email and password you chose at signup
  • The platform scopes everything to your entity — you only see your board
  • No new account, no separate password
01 · SIGN UP02 · KIT03 · CLAIM04 · CONNECTED05 · COCKPIT
Credentials go straight to /IOTCONNECT; the cockpit never stores them.

Your board, live

Card 1 — telemetry becomes gauges

  • Board telemetry as live gauges — CPU, temperature, memory, disk
  • The same ~50 attributes, updated every 10 s — now visual
  • The cockpit's cards are numbered in workshop order — scroll top to bottom and you exercise the board step by step

Ask your board

Card 2 — first prompts, every answer measured

  • LLM / Agent / VLM tabs — answers arrive with live load / TTFT / tok/s
  • The agent answers from real board data — time, temperature, memory — not guesses
  • First answer pays the model load (~1 min); it's a metric, not a bug

Model shootout

Cards 3 & 4 — pick a model and backend, then race every engine

  • Model & backend: switch models, run on CPU / Neutron / Ara240
  • Shootout: one prompt, every engine — load / TTFT / tok/s + each verbatim answer
  • The honest way to see what quantization, an NPU, or a bigger model buys

Teach it your docs

Card 5 — a knowledge base you feed yourself

  • Drop a PDF or document, or index a web page URL
  • Converted in the cloud, then chunked & embedded on the board
  • RAG on → grounded answers that quote your docs, verbatim

Voice, the finale

Card 6 — four models in a row, fully offline

  • “Hey NXP” → wake word → STT → LLM → TTS — no cloud in the loop
  • Every spoken exchange lands in telemetry — question, answer, count
  • The live workshop closes here

What you leave knowing

Four ideas the whole flow was built to teach

tok/s is a bandwidth story

Every token reads essentially all the weights once — speed is memory-bandwidth-bound.

Quantize, then re-validate

4-bit is survivable with mixed precision, brutal without it.

Ground or agent small models

RAG retrieves real passages; an agent runs a real tool — both beat guessing.

Measure load separately

Load, TTFT and tok/s are three numbers — never bury load in throughput.

Return to these in the wrap-up. Board goes back; the /IOTCONNECT account, dashboard, and RAG docs stay theirs.
